metadata.schedule_summary: Cycle 1 lasts 42 days: nivolumab, ipilimumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 1; nivolumab, paclitaxel and carboplatin on Day 22. These are the only two planned chemotherapy administrations. From Cycle 2, nivolumab is given on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1. Continue while appropriate until progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression. Your team reviews the plan and may delay or stop treatment.

indications.description: First-line metastatic squamous NSCLC without sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation.

treatment.schedule_summary: Cycle 1 only: paclitaxel/carboplatin on Days 1 and 22. Nivolumab Days 1 and 22; ipilimumab Day 1 every 42 days, to progression, unacceptable toxicity or up to 24 months without progression.

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.label: Worst relevant non-haematological toxicity

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No other non-haematological adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Grade 1 under the named CTCAE term: generally mild or asymptomatic, with observation only and no intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Grade 2 under the named CTCAE term: generally moderate; local/non-invasive intervention may be indicated and instrumental activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Grade 3 under the named CTCAE term: severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated and self-care activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Grade 4 under the named CTCAE term: life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify the exact adverse event, grade it with its own CTCAE criteria and assess functional impact before selecting a grade.
other_nonhaem_toxicity_grade.source_grading_note: Use the exact event and source CTCAE v4; no generic grade establishes immune attribution.

neuropathy_grade.label: Peripheral neuropathy grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No peripheral sensory or motor neuropathy.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only. CTCAE v4.0 grades symptomatic paraesthesia separately when that is the more accurate term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate symptoms that limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms that limit self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening neurological consequences; urgent intervention required.

neuropathy_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess persistent sensory or motor symptoms, gait, dexterity and effect on activities of daily living.
neuropathy_grade.source_grading_note: Use the exact event and source CTCAE v4; no generic grade establishes immune attribution.

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion or hypersensitivity reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess timing, airway or haemodynamic compromise, treatment required and whether infusion interruption was needed.
infusion_reaction_grade.source_grading_note: Use the exact event and source CTCAE v4; no generic grade establishes immune attribution.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No pneumonitis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms; oxygen indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening respiratory compromise; urgent intervention such as ventilatory support required.

pneumonitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms, oxygen requirement, imaging and exclude infection/alternative causes.
pneumonitis_grade.source_grading_note: Use the exact event and source CTCAE v4; no generic grade establishes immune attribution.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated diarrhoea/colitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: Neither diarrhoea nor colitis is present.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Diarrhoea: fewer than 4 stools/day above baseline or mild ostomy-output increase. Colitis: asymptomatic, clinical/diagnostic observations only.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Diarrhoea: 4-6 stools/day above baseline or moderate ostomy-output increase; limits instrumental ADL. Colitis: abdominal pain or mucus/blood in stool.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Diarrhoea: at least 7 stools/day above baseline, incontinence, hospitalisation or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care ADL. Colitis: severe abdominal pain or peritoneal signs.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening diarrhoea or colitis; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess stool frequency over baseline, abdominal pain, blood/mucus, hydration, sepsis and peritoneal signs.
diarrhoea_colitis_grade.source_grading_note: Use the exact event and source CTCAE v4; no generic grade establishes immune attribution.

rash_grade.label: Immune-mediated rash/dermatitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No rash. Use the most specific CTCAE skin term when a rash is present.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: For maculopapular rash: under 10% body-surface area, with or without symptoms such as itch, burning or tightness.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: For maculopapular rash: 10–30% body-surface area, or rash limiting instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: For maculopapular rash: over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, or limitation of self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Grade 4 is not defined for uncomplicated maculopapular rash; use the appropriate severe cutaneous-reaction term if life-threatening features are present.

rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess morphology, body-surface area, symptoms, mucosal involvement and functional impact.
rash_grade.source_grading_note: Use the exact event and source CTCAE v4; no generic grade establishes immune attribution.

eligibility: First-line metastatic squamous NSCLC in adults without sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation.
ECOG 0–2; adequate organ function; exact source eligibility and caution review.
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
Regimen-specific exclusions encoded in the interactive assessment
monitoring: Baseline FBC, renal/liver profile, glucose and TFTs; hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C RNA. GFR for carboplatin; audiology/CrCl and neuropathy assessment when indicated.
FBC and renal/liver before each treatment; glucose/TFTs before each 42-day cycle.
Cortisol when clinically indicated. Disease monitoring follows consultant plan.
Immune toxicity surveillance through treatment and at least five months after last immune dose.
dose_modifications: Source CTCAE v4; hold or stop both immune drugs jointly, never immune dose reductions. Isolated laboratory abnormalities do not establish immune causation.
Distinguish chronic organ impairment from active immune hepatitis/nephritis. Stable impairment no-adjustment wording does not authorise treatment without assessment.
Paclitaxel 200→150→100 mg/m²; carboplatin AUC6→5→4; third reduction discontinue. Resolve concurrent limitations without multiplying reductions.
Source ANC/platelet overlaps and hepatic decimal gaps are explicit review pathways.
